requirements.quote:
QUIC carries TLS handshake data in CRYPTO frames, each of which
   consists of a contiguous block of handshake data identified by an
   offset and length.
requirements.condition: When QUIC carries TLS handshake data.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the TLS handshake data in CRYPTO frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not carry TLS handshake data as another frame type.
requirements.why_checkable: A generated packet trace can be inspected to verify that TLS handshake bytes are carried in CRYPTO frames.

requirements.quote:
QUIC carries TLS handshake data in CRYPTO frames, each of which
   consists of a contiguous block of handshake data identified by an
   offset and length.
requirements.condition: For each CRYPTO frame carrying TLS handshake data.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the frame payload as a contiguous block of handshake data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not represent discontiguous handshake-data regions as one CRYPTO-frame block.
requirements.why_checkable: The data range described by a decoded CRYPTO frame can be checked for contiguity.

requirements.quote:
QUIC carries TLS handshake data in CRYPTO frames, each of which
   consists of a contiguous block of handshake data identified by an
   offset and length.
requirements.condition: For each CRYPTO-frame block of handshake data.
requirements.required_behavior: Identify the block by an offset.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit the offset identifying the block.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoded CRYPTO frame exposes whether its offset is encoded and identifies its data position.

requirements.quote:
QUIC carries TLS handshake data in CRYPTO frames, each of which
   consists of a contiguous block of handshake data identified by an
   offset and length.
requirements.condition: For each CRYPTO-frame block of handshake data.
requirements.required_behavior: Identify the block by a length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit the length identifying the block.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoded CRYPTO frame exposes whether its length is encoded and matches the represented data block.

requirements.quote:
Those frames are packaged into QUIC packets and
   encrypted under the current encryption level.
requirements.required_behavior: Package the CRYPTO frames into QUIC packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transmit CRYPTO frames outside QUIC packets.
requirements.why_checkable: Wire output can be decoded to verify that each sent CRYPTO frame is contained in a QUIC packet.

requirements.quote:
Those frames are packaged into QUIC packets and
   encrypted under the current encryption level.
requirements.condition: When sending a QUIC packet containing CRYPTO frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Encrypt it under the current encryption level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not protect it with an encryption level other than the current level.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint's current encryption level and the keys that successfully decrypt the emitted packet can be compared.

requirements.quote:
As with TLS over TCP,
   once TLS handshake data has been delivered to QUIC, it is QUIC's
   responsibility to deliver it reliably.
requirements.condition: Once TLS has delivered handshake data to QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Deliver that handshake data reliably.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not abandon handshake data merely because its containing packet was lost.
requirements.error_behavior: Recover from loss using QUIC reliability mechanisms.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss-injection test can determine whether handed-off TLS handshake data is eventually delivered despite packet loss.

requirements.quote:
Each chunk of data that is
   produced by TLS is associated with the set of keys that TLS is
   currently using.
requirements.condition: When TLS produces a chunk of data.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate that chunk with the set of keys TLS is currently using.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not associate the chunk with a different key set.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation can compare each produced chunk's stored encryption-level association with TLS's active keys at production time.

requirements.quote:
If QUIC needs to retransmit that data, it MUST use
   the same keys even if TLS has already updated to newer keys.
requirements.condition: If QUIC retransmits TLS-produced data after or before a TLS key update.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the same keys associated with the data when it was produced.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retransmit the data using newer keys selected by a subsequent TLS update.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can force loss across a key transition and verify which key set decrypts the retransmitted data.

requirements.quote:
Some frames are prohibited in different packet number spaces; see
   Section 12.5 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
requirements.condition: When placing frames into packets from different packet number spaces.
requirements.required_behavior: Observe the frame restrictions defined by QUIC-TRANSPORT Section 12.5.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place a prohibited frame in a packet number space where it is disallowed.
requirements.why_checkable: The quoted text does not identify the prohibited frame and packet-number-space combinations; the referenced external text is required to form concrete checks.

requirements.quote:
Because packets could be reordered on the wire, QUIC uses the packet
   type to indicate which keys were used to protect a given packet, as
   shown in Table 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the packet type to indicate which keys protected the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not emit a packet type inconsistent with the keys used to protect the packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet type and the key set that authenticates and decrypts a captured packet can be compared.

requirements.quote:
When packets of different types need to be sent,
   endpoints SHOULD use coalesced packets to send them in the same UDP
   datagram.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint needs to send packets of different types.
requirements.required_behavior: Use coalesced packets to send the different packet types in the same UDP datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: Given simultaneous need to send multiple packet types, emitted UDP datagrams can be inspected for coalescing.

requirements.quote: | Initial             | Initial secrets | Initial          |
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the packet using Initial secrets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not protect an Initial packet using another encryption-key category.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet type and key set that decrypts and authenticates the packet can be compared with the table mapping.

requirements.quote: | Initial             | Initial secrets | Initial          |
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Initial packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use another packet number space for an Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-number state and acknowledgments for an Initial packet can be checked against the Initial space.

requirements.quote: | 0-RTT Protected     | 0-RTT           | Application data |
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the packet using 0-RTT keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not protect a 0-RTT Protected packet using another encryption-key category.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet type and key set that decrypts and authenticates the packet can be compared with the table mapping.

requirements.quote: | 0-RTT Protected     | 0-RTT           | Application data |

requirements.required_behavior: Protect the packet using Handshake keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not protect a Handshake packet using another encryption-key category.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet type and key set that decrypts and authenticates the packet can be compared with the table mapping.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use another packet number space for a Handshake packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-number state and acknowledgments for a Handshake packet can be checked against the Handshake space.

requirements.quote: | Retry               | Retry           | N/A              |
requirements.required_behavior: Use Retry-specific protection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not protect a Retry packet using another encryption-key category.
requirements.why_checkable: A Retry packet's integrity protection can be compared with the table's Retry protection category.

requirements.quote: | Retry               | Retry           | N/A              |
requirements.required_behavior: Do not assign the packet to a packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not consume or track a packet number for a Retry packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation state can be inspected to verify that Retry processing does not use a packet number space.

requirements.quote: | Version Negotiation | N/A             | N/A              |
requirements.required_behavior: Do not use encryption keys to protect the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply an encryption-key category to a Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized packet can be checked for the absence of cryptographic protection associated with an encryption-key category.

requirements.quote: | Version Negotiation | N/A             | N/A              |
requirements.required_behavior: Do not assign the packet to a packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not consume or track a packet number for a Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation state can be inspected to verify that Version Negotiation processing does not use a packet number space.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not protect a Short Header packet using another encryption-key category.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet type and key set that decrypts and authenticates the packet can be compared with the table mapping.
